To determine whether the sequence converges or diverges, we need to determine the limit of the sequence as $n$ approaches infinity:

$$
{lim}_{n\to \infty }{a}_{n}={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{-8n+7}{4n}.
$$

The dominant term in the denominator is $4n,$ so we divide the numerator and the denominator by $n$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{n\to \infty }{a}_{n} & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{-8n+7}{4n} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{-8n}{n}+\frac{7}{n})}{\frac{4n}{n}} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{-8+\frac{7}{n}}{4} \\  & =\frac{-8+0}{4} \\  & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, the sequence converges, and its limit is $-2.$
